answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate combined with incumbent's refusal to negotiate leaves switch_primary_vendor as the only path to meet the financial constraint. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor delivered quick onboarding and accurate invoicing when moved to primary supply previously. memory_c4 shows negotiation recovered margin, but the incumbent has already refused this cycle, eliminating that option. The assembly line is at 94% utilization with no buffer, making add_second_source insufficient to meet the cost target and creating dual-source complexity during a tight delivery window. Deferring is impossible given the 14-day expiration and no auto-renewal. However, verifying memory_c2 (low-cost vendor track record) and memory_c4 (prior negotiation limits) will confirm whether the low-cost vendor can sustain primary supply quality under higher volume and whether there is any negotiation angle we have not yet explored. The standard_experiment scale acknowledges the onboarding risk is non-zero even with prior success, and allows early detection of invoicing or delivery anomalies before full commitment.
